chosen: Adopt Rauthy (Rust, Apache-2.0) rather than build an identity server: sign-in, passkeys, roles, groups, an admin screen and the agents' keys come with it, and this repo holds its deployment and the agents' setup (your answer on TK-91).
Rauthy answers at `auth.bendelhome.cc`, on the LAN and over Tailscale like tickets, behind the gateway's proxy over HTTPS (your answer).

Rauthy keeps its data in the gateway's shared Postgres: it connects like any stack, gets a database and a role of its own, and the nightly dumps back it up (your answer, from your question "can we use shared postgres?").
Rauthy sends no mail for now: you read a sign-in or reset link from its log when you need one, and a mail relay comes when a second person signs in (your answer).

Its secrets (the encryption keys, the first admin's password) stay out of git, in the deploy's environment.

plan.title: Deploy it as a stack on the gateway, at auth.bendelhome.cc over HTTPS
plan.description:
The live gateway runs it like its other stacks, connected to the shared Postgres (its form's Shared services), which makes its database and role, behind its proxy with a certificate, at `auth.bendelhome.cc` (a Caddy connection, as the apps' addresses are), on the LAN and over Tailscale only, like tickets (chosen on AU-1). Passkeys need HTTPS and an address that doesn't change.

Settings, from building AU-1.1:

- The stack is named `auth` and its service `rauthy`, since the gateway hands Postgres in as `GW_rauthy__PG*`; the Caddy connection points at service `rauthy`, port 8080.
- `TRUSTED_PROXIES` is `shared-caddy`'s subnet, read on the machine. If that network is ever made again, every request is refused until it's updated.
- No mail relay for now (chosen on AU-1): `SMTP_URL` stays unset, so Rauthy writes its sign-in and reset links to its log, where you read one when you need it. A relay comes when a second person signs in.
- The image has no shell, so there's no healthcheck: a deploy counts on the container staying up through the gateway's 10-second watch.

It changes the live gateway, so it's yours to run.

plan.title: Check a restore from the nightly dump, and keep the encryption keys apart from it
plan.description: The shared Postgres dumps Rauthy's database each night, a week kept (chosen on AU-1), with its people, apps, agents and signing keys. The signing keys are stored encrypted with Rauthy's encryption keys, which live in the deploy's environment: without them a dump can't be read, so they're kept safe, and apart from the dumps. A restore is tried once, on a copy: a person signs in and an agent gets a token.

plan.title: Update the README and `.env.example`: Rauthy makes the first admin's password, and the gateway the encryption key
plan.description: No docker command is left in the steps. `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD_ARGON2ID` becomes optional and stays unset: Rauthy makes the first admin's password on its first start and prints it in its log (Rauthy's config reference: "random -> see logs on first start"), read once on the stack's log to sign in and add the passkey (AU-1.4). `ENC_KEYS` is made by the gateway's Make in Rauthy's shape (GW-17.1), and `ENC_KEY_ACTIVE` is its id, `k1`. `TRUSTED_PROXIES` on the gateway is `172.31.0.0/16`, `shared-caddy`'s subnet; the example's `172.30.0.0/16` is a placeholder. The config's `[bootstrap]` comment says the same.

plan.title: Set the stack's last variables: the encryption key the gateway makes, its id, and the first admin's email
plan.description: The `auth` stack is on the live gateway since 2026-10-13, made from this repo's `main` with deploy on push off: its Postgres connection (database and role `auth`), its Caddy connection (`auth.bendelhome.cc`, port 8080), `TRUSTED_PROXIES` (`172.31.0.0/16`) and both `HQL_SECRET_*`, made by the gateway. This adds `ENC_KEYS` (`make: {bytes: 32, encoding: 'base64', prefix: 'k1/'}`), `ENC_KEY_ACTIVE` (`k1`) and `BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL` (your email), sending every variable, since a `PATCH` takes the whole set. Done from your gateway session, with your permission.
